scope: the retained training support of the household panel. No reserved split is read

acf.name: autocorrelation function with one whole-series denominator
acf.formula: sum over the admitted offsets of (x_i - xbar)(x_{i+k} - xbar), divided by the sum over every admitted position of (x_i - xbar)^2, with xbar the mean of the admitted positions. The denominator does not shrink with k while the numerator does
acf.retained_implementation: tools/df_e1_data_audit.py::autocorrelation — the estimator the published four-row list was produced by

pearson.name: Pearson correlation over lag-truncated pairs
pearson.formula: the two legs of the admitted pairs, each centred and scaled on its own pair count: cov(a, b) / (sd(a) sd(b)). Every admitted pair is weighted once and nothing is divided by a population it was not measured on
pearson.retained_implementation: np.corrcoef(v[:-k], v[k:]) as tools/df_rp49_rp64_audit.py::data_audit computes it

populations.positions_deleted_before_the_offsets: the non-finite position is removed from the series and the offsets are applied to what remains, so every pair straddling the removal is really k+1 minutes apart and is counted as k. This is the population BOTH superseded versions used
populations.offsets_on_the_retained_clock_under_a_fi: the retained one-minute grid is left intact, the offsets are applied on it, and a pair is admitted only when both of its legs are finite. An index separation of k IS a separation of k minutes for every admitted pair

supersedes.what: the four-row autocorrelation list of SATOSHI_PROGRAM_RP57_RP64_RETURN_2026_09_21 (RP59) and the `autocorrelation.autocorrelation_by_lag_minutes` block of docs/audits/evidence/d3_k5_20260917/RP59/DATA_TARGET_PREPROCESSING_AUDIT.json
supersedes.estimator: autocorrelation function with one whole-series denominator
supersedes.defect: two defects. The estimator was not named, and its denominator does not shrink with the offset while its numerator does, so the printed sequence reads as a decay that is partly the estimator. And the population deleted a position before applying the offsets, so some pairs counted as k minutes apart are k+1
supersedes.withdrawn: nothing. The values are correct arithmetic on the population and estimator they used, both of which are now named beside them

supersedes.what: the `bias_corrected` column of docs/audits/evidence/RP59_LAG_AND_SPLITS_20260926/LAG_TABLE_AND_SPLIT_MATERIALIZATION.json and the table of SATOSHI_RP59_LAG_TABLE_AND_MATERIALIZATION_2026_09_26.md §1.2, at satoshi/rp59-lag-table-restatement-20260926 tip 6820fcae
supersedes.defect: two defects. It kept the deleting population it inherited, so it corrected an estimator while leaving the clock compressed; and it called its column 'bias-corrected', which names a Pearson correlation as if it were the published autocorrelation function rescaled. It is not: the rescaled autocorrelation function and the Pearson correlation differ, and this tool publishes both so the claim can be checked rather than believed
supersedes.withdrawn: the label 'bias-corrected' is withdrawn. The numbers are retained, labelled by the estimator and the population that produced them

not_a_window_selector.this_table_is: an ordering of the LINEAR dependence between the target and its own past at four offsets, measured on the retained training support of one household panel
not_a_window_selector.this_table_is_not: a context-window selector. It does not rank candidate windows, it does not measure the conditional contribution of a lag to a predictor, and it does not say that a weekly context improves a forecast. No model was fitted to produce any number in it
not_a_window_selector.the_inversion_specifically: the week standing above the day is a fact about marginal linear dependence at two offsets. A prefix that includes a weekly offset must be justified by measured skill under the programme's own protocol, not by this ordering

is_this_training: no. Reanalysis of retained bytes: nothing is fitted, built or scored

support.note: the deleting population's row count is the published support. The clock has one more position than that, and the correction keeps it

pearson_is_not_the_rescaled_autocorrelat.claim: the Pearson correlation over lag-truncated pairs is NOT the autocorrelation function with one whole-series denominator rescaled by n/(n-k). The earlier restatement's 'bias-corrected' label asserted an equivalence that does not hold

what_the_deleting_population_cost.reading: the shift is small in magnitude and it is not the point: a population that counts pairs at the wrong offset is wrong whatever the size of the consequence, and its size could not be known before it was measured

day_versus_week_inversion.claim: the day-versus-week inversion: the weekly offset carries MORE marginal linear dependence than the daily one, reversing the order the published list printed
day_versus_week_inversion.and_still_not_a_selector: the week standing above the day is a fact about marginal linear dependence at two offsets. A prefix that includes a weekly offset must be justified by measured skill under the programme's own protocol, not by this ordering

the_reading_that_survives_unchanged.claim: the daily offset carries less marginal linear dependence than the hourly one, so a daily context remains a hypothesis and not a certainty

clock.why_this_check_exists: a finite-pair mask keeps the offsets honest only if the retained rows are a gapless grid at the declared step. If they were not, the repair would have to carry the stamps, not the indices
